Independent replay method: over Q(h), form A=6I-4hQ+h^2 Q^2 and B=6I+2hQ, multiply B by adj(A), then divide each first-row offset j numerator by h^j and verify row-sum numerator det(A); test rational signs and positive root counts with exact Sturm sequences.
correctness.rationale: Since the spectrum of h(S-I) lies in the closed left half-plane and both poles are in the right half-plane, the map exists for every h>=0. Applying it to the constant vector yields row sum R(0)=1. The residue at 2+i sqrt(2) is 1-5i sqrt(2)/2; expanding the inverse in cyclic powers gives the stated numerator formula over |(h+2+i sqrt(2))^n-h^n|^2>0. Circulant shifts occupy disjoint positions in each row, so at h>0 each offset sign is exactly its reduced numerator sign. Independent exact symbolic matrix inversion and Sturm checks reproduced the polynomials and classifications for 2<=n<=8. For 2–5 all reduced numerators have nonnegative coefficients and positive constants. For 6 and 7 the diagonals stay positive and the last offset threshold dominates; the required roots are isolated in (0.208,0.209) and (0.663,0.664), respectively. At 8, offsets 5–7 each have one positive root, with the offset-7 root alpha largest. The diagonal has exactly two positive roots, with rational brackets (3.297,3.298) and (7.042,7.043) and sign changes + to - and - to +. Thus the admissible positive steps are exactly [alpha,beta] and [gamma,infinity), including all three endpoints by nonnegativity. At h=0 the map is the identity in every dimension. The independent check was exact, not timestepping on a numerical grid.
residual_risks: Endpoint entrywise nonnegativity is not strict positivity of every entry at a boundary, internal-stage positivity, or a time-discretization accuracy guarantee. The complete classification stops at n=8.

value.rationale: An exact sign phase diagram for a canonical method on directed Markov cycles distinguishes a genuine two-window domain from a few illustrative sample steps. Certifying that the immediately smaller cycle has one recovery interval settles where the first nonmonotone phase diagram occurs; the three precise boundaries tell which timesteps actually preserve stochasticity in that first dimension.
